history.summary: CONFIRMED but FLAG AMBIGUITY: this is the Dhwaj Temple on Dhwaj peak near Pithoragarh (Shiva + Goddess Jayanti), not to be confused with the 9th-century 'Dhawaj'/Kachheri Temple at Dwarahat (permanently closed; reported ~78 km away). 'Dhwaj' means flag - the peak is a local symbol of divine presence; legend says the place was named 'Dhwaja' in Shiva's honour by ancestors of the Kapdi clan, that a ~50-ft cave here was the abode of Shiva/Khandnath, and (weakly sourced) that Adi Shankaracharya built it and the Pandavas visited in exile. A cave Shiva temple lies ~200 ft below the main shrine. The temple sits at ~2,100 m with panoramic views of Nanda Devi, Trishul and Panchachuli. COORDINATES APPROXIMATE (verify): 29.647554, 80.288363 comes from a place-listing record, not a verified POI match; road distance to Pithoragarh is reported as 10 km or 18 km and the trek as 3-8 km (CONFLICT, verify).

name: Dhwaj Temple
town_description: Pithoragarh is a hill town in the Kumaon Himalayas (~1,645 m), district headquarters of Pithoragarh district and a historic town of the Chand kings with the Gakhul Ghat-style Pithoragarh Fort. It is the gateway to the Kailash-Mansarovar and Himalayan trek routes of eastern Uttarakhand.

travel.airport: Naini Saini Airport, Pithoragarh, ~10 km (uktravelcompany; chardhamtours cites Pantnagar, ~213 km - CONFLICT, verify)
travel.road: ~10-18 km from Pithoragarh town (CONFLICT), then a 3-8 km uphill trek from the Totanaula/Lalku base (2-3 hours; CONFLICT across sources)

visitor_information.best_time: March-June and September-November; Maha Shivratri and Navratri draw thousands; avoid monsoon (slippery trails, landslides)
visitor_information.opening_hours: Daylight hours daily; free entry (verify locally); local belief asks visitors to observe satvik food for 7 days before visiting (per traveller reviews)
